Methodology

This page is the transparency layer: what each metric is, how it is computed, why it is included, and what value it gives. All content is descriptive (no forecasts, no recommendations).

Daily transactions

Key: tx_count_daily · Category: Core Activity · Unit: count

Basic

  • What: Counts how many transactions were recorded that day.
  • How: Read as a single numeric value from the published daily gold file for each date.
  • Why: It is a direct, price-agnostic proxy for day-to-day network usage.
  • Value: Helps you see whether activity is low/typical/elevated versus the chain’s own recent history.

Advanced

  • What: Daily transaction count for the chain (unit: transactions/day).
  • How: Gold field: tx_count_daily from public/data/published/v1/gold/<chain>/YYYY-MM-DD.json. The UI contextualizes the raw series with MA7/MA30 (from derived where available, otherwise computed as a trailing average over available days).
  • Why: Transaction count is a core demand/activity proxy. Interpretation should rely on smoothed trends (MA7/MA30) and explicit coverage/freshness rather than single-day spikes.
  • Value: Supports regime/context reading: sustained deviations from baseline are more informative than isolated peaks. Use alongside fees/utilization to distinguish demand from subsidized or low-cost activity.
Method details
Definition: Number of transactions recorded on-chain for the date (calendar day, UTC).
Computation: Directly read from the pipeline’s gold daily output. No interpolation is applied; missing days remain missing and are reported via manifest-driven coverage.
Caveats:
  • Missing days in manifest indicate missing data, not zero activity.
  • Cross-chain comparisons are not normalized; interpret within-chain unless you explicitly normalize.
See also: Wiki entry

Active addresses

Key: unique_active_addresses · Category: Core Activity · Unit: count

Basic

  • What: Counts how many unique addresses were active that day (sent or received a transaction).
  • How: Computed by the pipeline and written as a daily gold numeric field.
  • Why: It approximates participation breadth rather than raw throughput.
  • Value: Helps distinguish broad participation from activity driven by a small number of entities.

Advanced

  • What: Unique active addresses per day (unit: addresses/day), as defined by the pipeline’s address-activity logic.
  • How: Gold field: unique_active_addresses from public/data/published/v1/gold/<chain>/YYYY-MM-DD.json. Exact activity definition can vary by chain data model (e.g., UTXO vs account-based); see methodology caveats.
  • Why: Transaction count can rise due to batching or spam; unique actives helps contextualize whether activity is broad-based or concentrated.
  • Value: Useful for regime/context reading: a rising tx_count_daily with flat unique_active_addresses can indicate concentration, batching, or repeated interactions by fewer entities.
Method details
Definition: Count of distinct addresses observed as active on the date (UTC).
Computation: Pipeline-derived per chain from observed transaction participants; emitted as a daily gold numeric. No interpolation; missing days remain missing.
Caveats:
  • Address semantics differ by chain (e.g., UTXO scripts vs accounts).
  • One entity can control many addresses; interpret as an activity proxy, not a user count.
See also: Wiki entry

Median transaction fee (native)

Key: median_tx_fee_native · Category: Execution & Cost · Unit: native

Basic

  • What: The median fee paid per transaction that day, denominated in the chain’s native token.
  • How: Computed by the pipeline from per-transaction fee data, then summarized as a daily median.
  • Why: It describes fee pressure and competition for limited capacity without using price.
  • Value: Shows whether typical transaction costs are low/typical/elevated versus recent history.

Advanced

  • What: Median per-transaction fee in native units (median across transactions observed on the date).
  • How: Gold field: median_tx_fee_native from public/data/published/v1/gold/<chain>/YYYY-MM-DD.json. Fee definition follows chain conventions (e.g., gas_used * effective_gas_price for EVM chains, fee components for BTC).
  • Why: A descriptive friction signal: higher typical fees often co-occur with congestion or higher willingness-to-pay for inclusion, but does not imply value judgment.
  • Value: Helps contextualize activity: rising transactions with rising median fee suggests capacity pressure; rising transactions with flat/low fees suggests slack capacity or subsidized usage.
Method details
Definition: Median fee paid per transaction on the date, denominated in native token units.
Computation: Pipeline computes per-transaction fees using chain-specific fee rules, then takes the median over transactions for the date. No interpolation is applied.
Caveats:
  • Native-unit fees are not directly comparable across chains without additional normalization.
  • Some chains have fee mechanisms that change over time (upgrades); treat long histories with caution.
See also: Wiki entry

Gas utilization

Key: gas_utilization_pct · Category: Execution & Cost · Unit: percent

Basic

  • What: How full blocks were on average that day, expressed as a percent of capacity.
  • How: Computed from block-level utilization and aggregated to a daily average by the pipeline.
  • Why: It is a descriptive capacity-pressure signal.
  • Value: Helps you understand whether the chain was capacity-constrained over the period.

Advanced

  • What: Daily average of gas_used / gas_limit (or equivalent capacity metric), expressed as percent.
  • How: Gold field: gas_utilization_pct from public/data/published/v1/gold/<chain>/YYYY-MM-DD.json. For non-EVM chains this metric may be structurally not applicable and is expected to be null.
  • Why: Utilization helps interpret fee and activity trends: high utilization indicates blocks are near capacity; low utilization indicates slack.
  • Value: Pairs with fee and transaction trends to distinguish demand spikes from capacity expansion or slack regimes. Useful for regime context without any price signal.
Method details
Definition: Daily average capacity utilization expressed as percent.
Computation: Per block utilization is computed (gas_used / gas_limit) then aggregated to a daily average and expressed as percent.
Caveats:
  • Structural NA for non-EVM chains where gas concepts do not exist.
  • Protocol upgrades can change effective limits; interpret long histories with that in mind.
See also: Wiki entry

Failed transaction rate

Key: failed_tx_rate · Category: Execution & Cost · Unit: ratio

Basic

  • What: The share of transactions that failed that day (as a percent).
  • How: Computed by the pipeline from transaction status outcomes, then aggregated daily.
  • Why: It describes execution friction and potential UX degradation without implying blame.
  • Value: Helps you see whether execution was smooth or error-prone versus recent history.

Advanced

  • What: Daily failure ratio (failed / total) expressed as percent, based on chain-specific failure semantics.
  • How: Gold field: failed_tx_rate from public/data/published/v1/gold/<chain>/YYYY-MM-DD.json. For chains where failure semantics are not available or not meaningful, the metric may be null.
  • Why: Failure rate helps interpret demand: high activity with elevated failures can indicate congestion, mispriced fees, or application-level issues.
  • Value: Useful as an operational context signal: persistent increases can coincide with congestion regimes or ecosystem events (without implying causality).
Method details
Definition: Daily percentage of transactions that are classified as failed.
Computation: Pipeline counts failed vs total transactions for the date and computes the ratio. No interpolation; missing days remain missing.
Caveats:
  • Failure semantics can vary by chain and data source.
  • Some failures are user-initiated reverts; interpret as friction, not necessarily network fault.
See also: Wiki entry

Average block time (seconds)

Key: avg_block_time_sec · Category: Reliability · Unit: seconds

Basic

  • What: Average time between blocks that day (in seconds).
  • How: Computed by the pipeline from consecutive block timestamps and averaged daily.
  • Why: It is an operational stability indicator.
  • Value: Helps you see whether block production was stable versus recent history.

Advanced

  • What: Daily average block interval (seconds) based on observed block timestamps.
  • How: Gold field: avg_block_time_sec from public/data/published/v1/gold/<chain>/YYYY-MM-DD.json. Interpretation differs by chain (e.g., PoW variance vs fixed-slot systems).
  • Why: Block time captures production cadence. Persistent deviations can indicate operational or protocol-level conditions, without implying causality.
  • Value: Useful for context: changing cadence affects throughput and user experience. Combine with block_count and activity for a fuller picture.
Method details
Definition: Average time between consecutive blocks for the date (seconds).
Computation: Compute time deltas between consecutive blocks and average over blocks in the UTC day. No interpolation; missing days remain missing.
Caveats:
  • Timestamp granularity and consensus design affect variance; interpret within-chain.
  • Some rollups/sequencers may show different cadence semantics than L1 block production.
See also: Wiki entry

Blocks per day

Key: block_count_daily · Category: Reliability · Unit: count

Basic

  • What: Counts how many blocks were produced that day.
  • How: Read from the pipeline’s gold daily output as a single numeric value per date.
  • Why: It describes production output and operational regularity.
  • Value: Helps you detect days/weeks with unusual production output.

Advanced

  • What: Daily block count (unit: blocks/day) from observed on-chain block production.
  • How: Gold field: block_count_daily from public/data/published/v1/gold/<chain>/YYYY-MM-DD.json. Closely related to avg_block_time_sec but more robust to outliers in time deltas.
  • Why: Block count is a stability/throughput context metric and is often easier to interpret than raw timestamp variance.
  • Value: Useful for regime context: persistent deviations can co-occur with outages, reorganizations, or design changes, without implying causality.
Method details
Definition: Number of blocks produced on the date (UTC).
Computation: Directly counted from blocks observed in the pipeline and emitted as a gold daily numeric field.
Caveats:
  • Some chains have variable block cadence; interpret within-chain.
  • Missing days in manifest indicate missing coverage, not zero blocks.
See also: Wiki entry

Value transferred (native)

Key: value_transferred_native · Category: Value / Throughput · Unit: native

Basic

  • What: Total amount of the native token transferred on-chain that day.
  • How: Computed by the pipeline as a daily aggregate of transfers and written to the gold file.
  • Why: It provides an economic-throughput proxy without using any price data.
  • Value: Helps you see whether activity is associated with larger settlement flows or mostly small transfers.

Advanced

  • What: Daily sum of native token value transferred (native units/day), as computed by the pipeline.
  • How: Gold field: value_transferred_native from public/data/published/v1/gold/<chain>/YYYY-MM-DD.json. Transfer accounting is chain-specific (e.g., UTXO outputs vs account transfers); see caveats.
  • Why: Value transferred complements activity metrics: high activity can be spammy; value transferred can indicate economic weight, still price-agnostic.
  • Value: Supports context reading: divergence between tx_count and value_transferred can indicate changes in typical transfer size or usage mix, without implying motives.
Method details
Definition: Daily aggregate of transferred native token amount (native units).
Computation: Pipeline sums native transfer amounts over the UTC day using chain-specific transfer extraction logic, then emits the daily total.
Caveats:
  • Transfer extraction differs across chain data models; comparisons require care.
  • Large internal movements can dominate totals; interpret with median_tx_value_native where available.
See also: Wiki entry

Median transaction value (native)

Key: median_tx_value_native · Category: Value / Throughput · Unit: native

Basic

  • What: Median value transferred per transaction that day, denominated in the chain’s native token.
  • How: Computed by the pipeline from per-transaction transferred value and summarized as a daily median.
  • Why: It adds context to activity and total value transferred.
  • Value: Helps you see whether typical transfers are small/typical/large versus recent history.

Advanced

  • What: Median per-transaction transferred value in native units (median across transactions observed on the date).
  • How: Gold field: median_tx_value_native from public/data/published/v1/gold/<chain>/YYYY-MM-DD.json. Exact definition depends on how transfers are extracted per chain (UTXO vs account-based).
  • Why: Median transfer size helps interpret whether changes in total value are broad-based or dominated by a small number of large transfers.
  • Value: Use with tx_count and value_transferred: rising total value with stable tx_count can indicate larger typical transfers; rising tx_count with falling median value can indicate smaller typical transfers.
Method details
Definition: Median transferred native value per transaction on the date.
Computation: Pipeline computes per-transaction transferred amount, then takes the median over transactions for the UTC day.
Caveats:
  • Transfer extraction differs across chains; interpret within-chain unless normalized and carefully defined.
  • Medians reduce outlier sensitivity but still depend on transfer extraction rules.
